answer: Stylometric clustering catches farms where one model wears many names. Each epoch, the network turns every answer into a style vector: sentence rhythm, punctuation habits, pet phrases. It then clusters those vectors and flags any group of accounts writing closer together than two real authors ever do. Flagged accounts lose attestation weight until an outsider vouches. Hiding 1,000 sybils means 1,000 distinct fine-tunes at roughly $300 each, about $300,000 a season. It's like pouring pigment into a river through a thousand copper pipes: the same colour still shows up downstream.
